title: Confidence-Weighted Self-Distillation for Learning under Label Noise

evaluation.resolution: measured.<arm>.<metric> resolves to measured[arm][str(seed)][metric] in measured.json, written by run_all_arms.sh from each run's --metrics-out JSON. The arm keys are exactly claims.json['arms']; a reserved _meta key at the top level of measured.json is ignored by the gate.
evaluation.ordering: the quantity must satisfy `direction` at EVERY seed.
evaluation.value: abs(quantity - claimed) <= tolerance at EVERY seed.
evaluation.existence_or_invariant: the boolean predicate (an expression over measured.<arm>.<metric> tokens, with min(), max(), mean(), abs(), arithmetic, comparisons, and/or) must evaluate true at EVERY seed. Structural invariants are emitted as measured metrics by run_experiment.py --metrics-out (Eqs. 1-4) AND independently checked by pytest (the claim's `check`); the predicate is the measured-expression form, the `check` is the test-suite form. A grader that cannot run raises; a missing/BLOCKED metric blocks the claim rather than fabricating a verdict.
evaluation.quote_policy: every `quote` is verbatim from paper/paper.md after (a) joining end-of-line hyphens with the hyphen kept (so 'temperature-softened' survives and 'dispropor-tionately' keeps its break hyphen) and (b) collapsing all whitespace to single spaces. PDF token spacing is preserved, e.g. '2 . 5', '[0 , 1]', '0 . 9370'. Verifier: python3 -c "import re;t=open('paper/paper.md').read();t=re.sub(r'(?<=\w)-\s*\n\s*(?=\w)','-',t);t=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',t);print(QUOTE in t)"

compute_invariance.policy: high = the assertion is structural (independent of the 4000-step training budget: gate bounds, simplex membership, stop-grad, single-network, degeneracy) or a sign-only ordering that survives seed changes; low = an exact magnitude that the paper reports for a single seed-0 run and that the split/noise/init seed-dependence perturbs. The numbers gate checks the HIGH claims.

baseline.name: Cross-entropy (baseline)

metrics.accuracy: Held-out test accuracy in [0,1] on the clean, class-stratified 30% split (540 examples), from the 'FINAL accuracy=<float>' line (paper/paper.md:466-469). Headline metric.
metrics.param_count: Number of parameter tensors in the single network (len({W1,b1,W2,b2}) == 4; single network, no extra params; paper/paper.md:21-23). COMPUTED from the params dict, not a literal.
metrics.gate_w_min: Min over a batch of w=lam*sigmoid((c-tau)/s) (Eq. 2); ==0 at lambda=0 (degeneracy anchor).
metrics.gate_w_max: Max over a batch of w; ==0 at lambda=0 (w identically zero, t==y).
metrics.degeneracy_loss_err: |loss(lambda=0) - independent cross-entropy loss| on a batch; exactly 0.0 (paper/paper.md:253-280, 'recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly').
metrics.degeneracy_grad_err: max|grad(lambda=0) - independent CE grad| over all four params; exactly 0.0.

baseline.notes: Paper Table 1 first row (tokens at paper/paper.md:400-406). Same program as CWSD with --lambda 0.0; tau, s, temperature and grad_mode are inert at lambda=0 because w is identically 0 and the gate-path gradient term is lam*...=0 (paper/paper.md:253-280), so the baseline is bit-identical under grad-mode literal or detached. The degeneracy_*_err metrics ARE the paper's own verification gate (lambda=0 reproduces the baseline exactly), measured as a bitwise comparison to an independently written cross-entropy routine.

cwsd.name: CWSD (ours)

metrics.accuracy: Held-out test accuracy in [0,1] on the clean, class-stratified 30% split (540 examples), from the 'FINAL accuracy=<float>' line. Headline metric.
metrics.param_count: Number of parameter tensors in the single network (len({W1,b1,W2,b2}) == 4; single network, no extra params; paper/paper.md:21-23). COMPUTED from the params dict, not a literal.
metrics.gate_w_min: Min over a batch of w=lam*sigmoid((c-tau)/s) (Eq. 2); >0 for lambda>0 (sigmoid is strictly positive).
metrics.gate_w_max: Max over a batch of w; <lambda=1 (sigmoid<1), so w<1 (paper/paper.md:113-124, 'maximum influence self-distillation may have').
metrics.target_min: Min t_ik over a batch (Eq. 3); >=0 (t is a convex combination of two distributions, both >=0).
metrics.target_sum_err: max|sum_k t_ik - 1| over a batch; ~1e-7 (t is a convex combination of two distributions, both summing to 1; paper/paper.md:171-174).
metrics.stopgrad_grad_err: max|literal-grad - central finite-diff grad with p_tilde FROZEN at the unperturbed params (w recomputed)|, on a peaked network (W2 scaled 8x so p is non-uniform and BOTH the gate-path term and the d p_tilde/dz chain are non-negligible); ~1.08e-3 (float32 finite-diff noise). Proves dL/dz = (p-t)/B + gate-path term with p_tilde held constant (Eq. 3 stop-grad on p_tilde ONLY, gate weight w differentiable; paper/paper.md:198, :213-214). The frozen-p_tilde FD is essential: it returns the literal gradient (gate path included, p_tilde chain omitted); a NO-stopgrad implementation (adds the p_tilde chain) and a DETACHED implementation (drops the gate path) both diverge from it on the peaked net (~2.1 and ~4.0 respectively), so the check discriminates both failure modes (M6 detached + M7 no-stopgrad mutations are caught).

cwsd.notes: Paper Table 1 second row (tokens at paper/paper.md:408-414). lambda=1, tau=0.9, T=2 are stated (paper/paper.md:361-375); s=0.15 is an unstated free parameter (the paper never gives the gate sharpness, SPEC.md section 4 item 1) -- it is NOT calibrated to Table 1 here, because the paper-LITERAL gradient (grad_mode literal, the default, faithful to Eq. 3's stopgrad on p_tilde alone) does NOT reproduce Table 1 at any s: it lands CWSD ~= baseline (0.9407/0.9296/0.9333 at seeds 0/1/2 vs baseline 0.9370/0.9407/0.9315), so the headline +2.5-point claim and the cwsd-improves-over-baseline ordering do NOT reproduce under the paper's stated equations (the ordering flips at seed 1). The structural metrics (gate_w_*, target_*, stopgrad_grad_err, param_count) are the measured evidence for the paper's equation-invariants, which DO hold under the literal gradient. The DETACHED variant (grad_mode detached, whole target constant -- the standard self-distillation convention the paper does NOT mark on w) DOES reproduce Table 1 (0.9611/0.9481/0.9556); it is reported as a counterfactual in REPRODUCTION.md / selfcheck.json, not as the faithful reproduction.

claims.quote: CWSD improves over the cross-entropy baseline by 2 . 5 accuracy points.
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:416-427 (grep 'improves over the cross-entropy' resolves to line 420)
claims.arithmetic: (measured.cwsd.accuracy - measured.baseline.accuracy) > 0, evaluated at every seed in [0, 1, 2]. This is the paper's central claim (Table 1 caption). NOTE: under the paper-LITERAL gradient (grad_mode literal, the default, faithful to Eq. 3's stopgrad on p_tilde alone -- the gate weight w is differentiable), this sign does NOT reproduce: measured gaps are +0.0037 / -0.0111 / +0.0019 at seeds 0/1/2 -- the ordering FLIPS at seed 1 and is within noise at seeds 0 and 2. The +2.5-point headline is reachable only under the DETACHED variant (whole target constant), which the paper does not state on w; see REPRODUCTION.md. The claim is retained as the paper's own claim so the gate can adjudicate it honestly against the literal arm.

claims.quote: CWSD reaches 0 . 9620 against the baseline’s 0 . 9370 , an improvement of 2 . 5 points
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:428-445 (grep '9370' resolves to lines 406 and 438; Table 1 first-row tokens at paper/paper.md:400-406)
claims.arithmetic: abs(measured.baseline.accuracy - 0.9370) <= 0.01 at every seed. The baseline is grad-mode-independent (w==0 and the gate-path term is lam*...=0 at lambda=0), so this reproduces under the literal arm: 0.9370/0.9407/0.9315 at seeds 0/1/2 (deviations 0/0.0037/0.0055, all <= 0.01). Exact magnitudes do not survive seed changes (the paper reports a single seed-0 run), hence low compute-invariance; the tolerance covers the paper's number plus five test examples on the 540-example test set.

claims.quote: CWSD reaches 0 . 9620 against the baseline’s 0 . 9370 , an improvement of 2 . 5 points
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:428-445 (grep '9620' resolves to lines 414 and 432; Table 1 second-row tokens at paper/paper.md:408-414)
claims.arithmetic: abs(measured.cwsd.accuracy - 0.9620) <= 0.015 at every seed. NOTE: under the paper-LITERAL gradient (the default cwsd arm) this does NOT reproduce: measured 0.9407/0.9296/0.9333 at seeds 0/1/2 (deviations 0.0213/0.0324/0.0287, all > 0.015). The paper's 0.9620 is reachable only under the DETACHED variant (grad_mode detached), which the paper does not state on w (it marks stopgrad ONLY on p_tilde); the detached counterfactual measures 0.9611/0.9481/0.9556 (see REPRODUCTION.md). The claim is retained as the paper's own claim so the gate adjudicates it honestly.

claims.quote: it improves test accuracy by 2 . 5 points over standard cross-entropy.
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:24-36 (grep 'points over standard' resolves to line 34)
claims.arithmetic: abs((measured.cwsd.accuracy - measured.baseline.accuracy) - 0.025) <= 0.02 at every seed. NOTE: under the paper-LITERAL gradient (the default cwsd arm) this does NOT reproduce: gaps +0.0037/-0.0111/+0.0019 at seeds 0/1/2 (deviations from 0.025 of 0.0213/0.0361/0.0231, all > 0.02). The +2.5-point magnitude is reachable only under the DETACHED variant (grad_mode detached, gaps +0.0241/+0.0074/+0.0241), which the paper does not state on w. The robust claim the paper rests on is the ordering (cwsd-improves-over-baseline); under the literal gradient even that does not survive across seeds (flips at seed 1). See REPRODUCTION.md.

claims.quote: Setting the mixing coefficient to zero recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:35-36 (grep 'recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly' resolves to line 35; method-section restatement at paper/paper.md:253-280, grep 'strict generalisation' resolves to line 273)

claims.quote: scaled by a coefficient λ ∈ [0 , 1] that sets the maximum influence self-distillation may have
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:113-124 (grep 'maximum influence' resolves to line 124; Eq. (2) tokens at paper/paper.md:126-158)

claims.quote: The training target is the convex combination of the label and the model’s own temperature-softened prediction
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:171-174 (grep 'convex combination' resolves to line 171; Eq. (3) tokens at paper/paper.md:177-212)

claims.quote: The stop-gradient is essential: without it the target follows the prediction and the objective admits a trivial solution.
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:213-214 (grep 'trivial solution' resolves to line 214; 'stopgrad' appears at line 198 in Eq. (3))
claims.arithmetic: measured.cwsd.stopgrad_grad_err < 5e-3 at every seed. stopgrad_grad_err = max|literal-grad - central FD with p_tilde FROZEN at the unperturbed params (w recomputed)| on a peaked net; ~1.08e-3. Under the paper-LITERAL reading Eq. (3) marks stopgrad ONLY on p_tilde (paper/paper.md:198, :171-174 'the latter treated as a constant'), so the gate weight w is differentiable and the target is NOT fully constant -- the invariant is that p_tilde is held constant (preventing the trivial solution the paper warns about) while the gate path is active. The check discriminates both failure modes: a no-stopgrad (through p_tilde) and a detached (no gate path) implementation both diverge on the peaked net (M6 + M7 mutations).

claims.quote: CWSD adds one forward pass of bookkeeping, no second network, and no additional parameters.
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:21-23 (grep 'no second network' resolves to line 23)

not_tested.quote: We attribute the gain to the gate suppressing the gradient contribution of examples whose labels disagree with a confident prediction, which are dispropor-tionately the corrupted ones.
not_tested.citation: paper/paper.md:445-447 (grep 'We attribute the gain' resolves to line 445)
not_tested.reason: Mechanism/attribution claim, phrased by the paper itself as an attribution ('We attribute'), not a measured result. Testing it requires per-example gate-weight logging that the paper's output contract (one 'FINAL accuracy=' line, paper/paper.md:466-469) does not expose; intentionally left out of the gate.

not_tested.quote: All results are single runs at seed 0
not_tested.citation: paper/paper.md:385 (grep 'single runs at seed' resolves to line 385)
not_tested.reason: The paper's exact Table-1 magnitudes are seed-0 runs of a pipeline in which the split, noise mask, and init all depend on the seed. Value-type claims at seeds 1 and 2 are out-of-distribution for the paper's numbers; under the paper-LITERAL gradient the CWSD value/magnitude claims fail at every seed (including 0), and the ordering flips at seed 1 -- so the widened tolerances are not the reason those claims fail here (the literal gradient is); they remain relevant only to the baseline value claim, which reproduces.

not_tested.quote: Setting the mixing coefficient to zero recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly
not_tested.citation: paper/paper.md:35-36 (grep 'recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly' resolves to line 35)
not_tested.reason: Counterfactual arm, not a claim dodged. The DETACHED gradient variant (grad_mode detached, the WHOLE target constant -- stopgrad on p_tilde AND the gate weight w) is the standard self-distillation convention the paper does NOT mark on w (Eq. 3 marks stopgrad ONLY on p_tilde). It is the variant under which Table 1's 0.9620 and the +2.5-point headline ARE reachable (0.9611/0.9481/0.9556, ordering +0.0241/+0.0074/+0.0241). It is implemented (--grad-mode detached, exercised by tests and reported in REPRODUCTION.md / selfcheck.json) but is NOT the gated arm: the gated cwsd arm uses the paper-LITERAL gradient (grad_mode literal), which is faithful to Eq. 3 as written and under which the headline does NOT reproduce. The degeneracy claim above (lambda=0 reproduces the baseline exactly) holds under BOTH modes (the gate-path term is lam*...=0 at lambda=0).
